title: A cellular thermal shift assay for detecting amino acid sites involved in drug target engagement
protocol: Wash cell culture plates twice with 2 mL ice-cold PBS.
Add 700 μL of ice-cold PBS to each plate.
Scrape adherent cells off the dishes using a cell scraper.
Divide cell suspensions from different groups into PCR tubes, placing 100 μL suspension per tube.
Heat the cell suspensions individually at 45°C for 5 min in a PCR amplifier.
Heat the cell suspensions individually at 48°C for 5 min in a PCR amplifier.
Heat the cell suspensions individually at 51°C for 5 min in a PCR amplifier.
Heat the cell suspensions individually at 58°C for 5 min in a PCR amplifier.
Heat the cell suspensions individually at 65°C for 5 min in a PCR amplifier.
Heat the cell suspensions individually at 69°C for 5 min in a PCR amplifier.
Determine the appropriate heating temperature and heating time through pre-experiments for different proteins or drugs.
Set a temperature gradient from 40°C to 70°C, with intervals of 2°C–3°C.
Incubate samples at each temperature for 3-6 hours while keeping incubation concentration constant.
Complete the full steps of the thermal shift assay to obtain a melting curve.
Choose the temperature where the protein is starting to degrade as the initial temperature point for later experiments.
Choose the temperature at which the protein is completely degraded as the ending temperature point.
Set the temperature interval usually between 5°C–7°C for subsequent experiments.
Optimize heating time similar to drug concentration optimization, typically setting it to 3-5 minutes.
Lysate heated cell suspensions with three cycles of freeze-thawing using liquid nitrogen and a 37°C water bath.
Centrifuge the lysed cells at 20,000 × g for 10 min at 4°C.
Isolate soluble fractions from the supernatant and transfer them to microcentrifuge tubes (about 80 μL per sample).
Determine the protein concentration using a Bradford assay.
Add 20 μL of 5 × loading buffer to the protein extraction.
Mix completely and boil at 95°C–100°C for 10 minutes.
Prepare pre-made (12% polyacrylamide) gels.
Load samples containing equal amounts of protein (10-50 μg/lane) into the lanes of the SDS-PAGE gels.
Include a molecular weight marker in one of the lanes to indicate the molecular weight.
Run the gels at 120 V for 1 to 2 hours until the bromophenol blue reaches the bottom of the gels.
Transfer protein from the gel into a PVDF membrane.
Wet a PVDF membrane in methanol for 30 seconds and then soak it in Transfer buffer.
Assemble the transfer sandwich starting with a sponge layer, followed by a filter paper layer, the gel layer, the PVDF membrane layer, another filter paper layer, and ending with a sponge layer.
Gently remove any air bubbles from the transfer sandwich layers to ensure no air bubbles are trapped.
Fill the transfer apparatus with Transfer buffer and place the transfer sandwich into it.
Run the wet transfer at 300 mA for 1 hour.
Rinse the PVDF membrane in TBST.
Incubate the membrane in Blocking solution for 2 hours at room temperature with gentle shaking.
Rinse the membrane briefly in TBST to remove residual milk.
Incubate the membrane with the primary antibody against Flag tag overnight (for 10–12 hours) at 4°C with gentle rocking.
Wash the membrane 3 times with TBST (10 minutes each with gentle rocking).
Incubate the membrane with HRP conjugated secondary antibody solution for 2 hours at room temperature with gentle rocking.
Wash the membrane 6 times with TBST (10 minutes each with gentle rocking).
Acquire the image and analyze the data.
Prepare the Chemiluminescent HRP Substrate mixture by mixing equal amounts of solution A and solution B provided by the manufacturer.
Incubate the membrane in the Chemiluminescent HRP Substrate mixture at room temperature for 10 seconds.
Expose the membrane with the chemiluminescent imaging system Clinx.
Optimize the incubation time for the substrate used.
Use LI-COR NIR secondary antibodies to avoid overexposure.
Determine the optimal exposure time using multiple exposure lengths.
Measure the band intensity using image analysis software such as Image J.
Calculate the relative band intensity.
Draw the cellular thermal shift assay curve using GraphPad.
Use total Flag-tagged CypA without any heating as loading controls.
Consider a housekeeping protein as an alternative for loading controls.
